title.narrative: Integrated Food Security and Protection Response, Including GBV Services, for Affected Populations in Far’ Al-Udayn district of Ibb governorate.

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThe project aligns with YHF SA1 2025 and aims to reduce morbidity and mortality by delivering prioritized, integrated, and multi-sectoral life-saving interventions. YWU seeks to build on its ongoing efforts in Ibb Governorate, particularly in Far' Al-Udayn district, by implementing a new project targeting 4938 vulnerable individuals, including women and children.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtSince 2018, YWU has partnered with UNHCR, UNFPA, and FAO in Ibb to provide protection, GBV, and food security services to IDPs and host communities. Under UNHCR funding, YWU has provided protection services to over 78,312 individuals, including case management, legal support, PSS, MPCA, protection cash assistance, and women's empowerment and livelihoods. Under UNFPA funding, YWU has provided 5,400 services to GBV survivors through their three established women’s safe spaces and a women’s shelter. In the food security sector, YWU has supported 80 households with livestock and training in modern livestock management techniques under UNHCR’s Quick Impact Project and has provided agricultural assets to more than 400 families with FAO funding.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project aims to address critical gaps caused by recent funding cuts from UNHCR and FAO and the closure of two UNFPA-supported safe spaces. Focusing on protection—particularly GBV—and food security, it targets vulnerable populations in Far' Al-Udayn. Through an integrated approach combining emergency relief, livelihood support, and protection services, the project seeks to enhance food security and provide life-saving assistance to those most in need.lt/pgtltpgtThe project aims to provide food security and livelihood interventions to 2170 vulnerable individuals (618 women, 512 girls, 570 men, and 470 boys). The project will distribute unconditional cash transfers to 230 HHs (1610 individuals) to ensure access to life-saving food assistance. Additionally, 560 individuals will benefit from livestock kits and cash plus assistance, promoting sustainable livelihoods and enhancing resilience. Capacity-building activities will include forming and training community committees, which will play a key role in identifying vulnerable beneficiaries, baseline and endline assessments, PDMs, providing community feedback, and ensuring the smooth implementation of activities.ltbrgtThe project also prioritizes the protection sector, focusing on delivering protection, human rights, and IHL monitoring, as well as case management and legal assistance to 2568 individuals (733 women, 568 girls, 746 men, and 521 boys) from both internally displaced and host communities, with particular emphasis on IDPs, who make up no less than 70%. Through the establishment of Community-Based Protection Networks (CBPNs), the project will ensure the provision of protection services, facilitate referrals, conduct community awareness sessions, and promote community participation in identifying the humanitarian protection needs of the community.ltbrgtFurthermore, GBV is a central concern of the project, which will provide multi-sectoral support to 200 GBV survivors. These services will include case management, cash assistance, livelihood skills training, and referrals. This holistic support ensures that GBV survivors can access essential services and begin rebuilding their lives.ltbrgtIn summary, this project seeks to provide a robust, integrated response to the crisis in Ibb Governorate, focusing on food security, protection, and GBV prevention and response. It aims not only to address immediate needs but also to foster resilience and empower the most vulnerable members of the community. YWU has established good access and experience in implementing projects in the target area and maintains strong relations with authorities and stakeholders. The project will be coordinated with FSAC and Protection Clusters to ensure smooth and efficient implementation and to avoid duplication.lt/pgt
